items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: this sub-area is almost entirely condos. The stock lines Quayside Drive from Westminster Pier Park east along the Waterfront Esplanade: the 2019 Bosa towers at the west end (RiverSky 1 and 2), the 1989–1990s Bosa-era towers mid-drive (Anchor Pointe, Riviera, Tiffany Shores, The Promenade), the Laguna Court cluster (Laguna Landing, The Excelsior), and the Aragon buildings at the Renaissance Square / Rialto Court pocket (The Q, Murano Lofts), plus two 1980s wood-frame low-rises (Quay West, Quayside Terrace).

Transit anchors: New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) at the top of the waterfront; TransLink route 103 is the Quayside / New Westminster Station route and route 102 serves Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station. Quayside Drive is the waterfront road; Columbia Street and 8th Street link the Quay to Downtown and the station, and Stewardson Way links west toward Marine Way and Burnaby.

Waterfront anchors: Westminster Pier Park at 600 Quayside Drive, Quayside Park (with a water play area) and the Waterfront Esplanade boardwalk run the length of the waterfront; a library kiosk and holds locker are at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, at the top of the waterfront.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quay condos

items.t: One developer built most of the waterfront, in two waves. Bosa built the first wave (Anchor Pointe 1989, Riviera 1990 per the building-data sources) and the current wave (RiverSky 1 and 2, both 2019; Pier West beside Pier Park) — cross-building comparisons of construction and warranty inside the Quay are unusually direct because so much stock shares one builder.

The Quay has two names and both are official in different places. The board sub-area name is "Quay" (SnapStats GVR); the City's heritage context name for the same neighbourhood is "Quayside," and the street, park and bus route all use Quayside. Searches under only one name miss records filed under the other.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Quay

items.t: Floodplain Zone 3 is the defining diligence item for Quayside stock — townhouse-form units included: the City's floodplain study places the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. For a ground-oriented townhouse unit at a tower's base, confirm the unit's own floor level against the building's Flood Construction Level compliance, plus the strata insurance and deductible position, before subject removal.

Form B diligence (every strata complex in, including RiverSky 2's townhouse units): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. A townhouse unit inside a tower strata is a strata lot like any other — there is no separate townhouse Form B.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quay townhomes

items.t: The Quay has a library presence without a branch: a library kiosk and holds locker sit at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, at the top of the waterfront, while the Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown.

The city's hospital is one SkyTrain ride east: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton (Fraser Health), east of the Quay by SkyTrain — relevant to the downsizer buyers this waterfront draws.

The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, fully opened in May 2024 — at 10,644 sq. m. the City's largest capital project to date, with an eight-lane 50-metre pool — and it sits up the hill from the Quay, not on the waterfront, despite how listings phrase it.

blocks.text: Quay home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

127 condos sold in Quay with a median price of $630,000 (the middle half sold between $545,000 and $731,000), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 97.3% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $632 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $591 a month.

faq.a: The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® counted 51 condos and townhomes listed in Quay at the end of October 2026. The number changes daily, so ask Jared for today’s count.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Quay?

faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Quay had a sales ratio of 14%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
faq.q: Is Quay a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 58 condos and townhomes sold in Quay over those 5 months, out of 327 in all of New Westminster.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Quay from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: Yes — the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. The practical questions are building-specific: flood construction level compliance, strata insurance cover and deductibles, and any flood-related claims history in the strata documents.
faq.q: Is the Quay in the floodplain?

faq.a: RiverSky 1 (908 Quayside Drive) and RiverSky 2 (988 Quayside Drive) were both built in 2019 by Bosa Properties — 33-storey concrete towers of 233 and 234 units.
faq.q: Which buildings are the newest, and does warranty remain?

faq.a: Mostly towers, but not all: Quay West (31 Reliance Court) is a 4-storey, 60-unit wood-frame low-rise built in 1986, Quayside Terrace (5 K de K Court) is a 4-storey building, and Murano Lofts (7 Rialto Court) is a 7-storey concrete mid-rise of 237 units built in 2005. Wood-frame versus concrete changes the insurance, depreciation-report and levy conversation — check which form the specific building is.
faq.q: Is there any low-rise or wood-frame stock, or is it all towers?

faq.a: Treat them as an unresolved conflict and verify the strata plan number on the specific unit's title before relying on either set of figures.
faq.q: The Riviera's address and year don't match between sources — which is right?

faq.a: No standalone one — the count is 0 strata and 0 fee-simple. The waterfront's stock is apartment stratas; the closest townhouse-form product is the TH-series homes at the base of RiverSky 2, which are strata lots inside that tower's plan (EPS5412).
faq.q: Is there a townhouse complex on the Quay?
What did condos in Quay sell for?
faq.a: 127 condos sold in Quay from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, at a median price of $630,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Quay?
faq.a: Typical time on the market was 28 days. At the median, sale prices were 97.3% of list, and 9% of sales closed above list (November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
